reasons_add: Ibn Isḥāq says Adam named every thing, and that each name remains attached to its thing until the Resurrection.

Al-Ṭabarī's possible reconstruction makes the challenge test an inference that exceeded what God had disclosed: the angels generalized from some corrupt descendants to all, while many obedient reformers were hidden from them. Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and al-Rabīʿ instead report that the challenge exposed a private boast about angelic knowledge and honor.
Al-Rabīʿ reports that God taught Adam the names to show his superiority over angels who had privately boasted of superior knowledge and honor.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda report that the angels' boast was private; al-Rabīʿ says the episode exposed both their public words and their hidden claim of superior knowledge and honor.

Al-Ṭabarī suspects a transmitter's error and reconstructs the report: the angels inferred that all descendants would corrupt from a statement concerning some, though God concealed the many who would obey, reform the earth and preserve blood. He expressly says this explains a possible report, not his chosen interpretation of the verse. He rejects the version in which God had already informed the angels of corruption and then reproached them for repeating it.
Al-Rabīʿ says Adam's taught names showed his superiority after angels had privately claimed that no creature would exceed their knowledge or honor.
Ibn ʿAbbās's report and al-Ṭabarī's continuation place Adam's naming after Iblis's refusal to prostrate and expulsion.
Ibn ʿAbbās's report and al-Ṭabarī's continuation set the angels' admission of limited knowledge beside God's disclosure of the pride Iblis had concealed.

Ibn ʿAbbās links Adam's haste to human impatience, illustrated by 17:11; the accounts say Adam praised God after sneezing, Iblis proudly refused prostration and was expelled, and Adam then named things.

Ibn ʿAbbās's report and al-Ṭabarī's continuation contrast the angels' disclaimer of unseen knowledge with Iblis's concealed pride; Ibn Isḥāq says their reply means they could answer only what God had taught them.

question: How long do the names Adam gave to things remain in use?

positions.position: The names Adam gave to things remain attached to those things until the Resurrection.
positions.reasons: Ibn Isḥāq says that Adam named every thing and that its name continues to be its name until the Resurrection.
